evals.prompt:
I ran the Figma MCP's get_design_context on the "PromoBanner" frame and got the response below. Please implement it as a Hearth React component.

Frame: PromoBanner
- Node "Banner Container" (Flex, direction: row)
  - Bound variable on its gap: layout/spacing/lg
  - Note: I checked this same frame at two breakpoints — the resolved pixel value for that variable was 24px on desktop and 16px on mobile, but it's the same bound variable both times.
  - Children:
    - Node "Icon" — component instance: StarMediumIcon. hidden: false.
    - Node "Label" — text, style "Body/Body Text MD". hidden: false.
    - Node "Muted subtitle" — text, style "Body/Body Text SM", content "Limited time only". hidden: true.
- No other children of Banner Container.

Please write the component.
evals.expected_output: A Flex container using the `spacing` prop (not `gap`) with the tier name `lg` — matched by the variable's name, not by copying either resolved pixel value (24px or 16px). The hidden "Muted subtitle" node is not rendered unconditionally; if it's included at all, the model raises it explicitly and asks for confirmation rather than silently rendering it as part of the default view.
expectations: Uses the `spacing` prop (not `gap`) on the Flex container, because the bound variable's path contains the segment "spacing"
Uses the tier name `lg` for the spacing prop, not a raw pixel value like 24 or 16
Does not treat the two different resolved pixel values (24px, 16px) as a reason to pick one over the other — matches by variable name only
Does not render the "Muted subtitle" text node unconditionally in the default view, since it is flagged hidden: true
If the hidden node is rendered at all, does so only with an explicit comment/flag and a question back to the user, not silently

evals.prompt:
Here's the design context for two Button instances in a row called "ActionRow". Implement them exactly as specified — no more, no less.

Frame: ActionRow
- Instance "Confirm Button" — component: Button. Props visible in the response: { variant: "solid" }. No colour/colorScheme variable is present in the response for this node.
- Instance "Cancel Button" — component: Button. Props visible in the response: { variant: "outline" }. No colour/colorScheme variable is present in the response for this node either.

Note: in the screenshot, "Cancel Button" looks like a slightly lighter/muted grey compared to "Confirm Button", but that's just how the outline variant renders against the background — there's no separate colour variable bound to either node.

Please implement both buttons.
evals.expected_output: Both buttons use only the variant prop given in the response (`solid` for Confirm, `outline` for Cancel). Neither gets an invented `colorScheme`/muted/secondary colour prop based on the screenshot's visual shading, since no colour variable was present in the response for either node.
expectations: Confirm Button is implemented with `variant="solid"` and no invented colour/colorScheme prop
Cancel Button is implemented with `variant="outline"` and no invented colour/colorScheme prop
Does not add a muted/secondary/faded colour variant to either button on the basis of the screenshot's visual shading alone
Does not treat the two instances as needing identical extra props just because they're the same component — each is implemented from its own listed props
